**Drift & Diffusion** is a modelling notebook. It is named after the two
terms of a stochastic differential equation: the *drift*, which is what the
system would do if nothing disturbed it, and the *diffusion*, which is
everything else. Most of the interesting physiology happens in the
conversation between the two.

Posts move along three axes:

- **Bayesian statistics**: inference as the updating of uncertainty, with
  algorithms written by hand before reaching for libraries.
- **Stochastic processes**: stochastic differential equations, state-space
  models and filtering.
- **Neuro-immuno-physiological modelling**: dynamical systems for autonomic
  control, inflammation and their couplings.

## Principles

Every post is a reproducible document: the text, the equations and the R
code behind each figure live in the same file. Models are deliberately
small, and simulated data are always labelled as such. Numbers quoted in
the text are computed at render time, never copied by hand.

## Colophon

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and R. The typeface is
Latin Modern, the family $\LaTeX$ sets by default, and equations are
rendered with $\KaTeX$. The palette is ink and paper, with two accents that carry meaning, as in
the equation on the front page: <span style="color: var(--accent)">ember</span>
for the drift and <span style="color: var(--accent2)">cyan</span> for the
diffusion.
